name: isaac_like
display_name: ISAAC-CE (32 nm analog ReRAM, Shafiee 2016 — SIMULATED)

validity.array_size_assumed: ISAAC-CE: 8 arrays of 128x128 2-bit cells per IMA, 8 ADCs per IMA, 12 IMAs per tile, 168 tiles
validity.notes: A DESIGN-SPACE STUDY, not a fabricated chip: areas and powers come from CACTI 6.5 at 32 nm plus published component models, and Table I reports POWER only — every energy constant here is derived by multiplying a published power by the paper's own 100 ns cycle and dividing by the printed instance count. The supply voltage is never stated. Treat this as a modelled design point.

area_per_cell.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I, memristor-array row, p.8
area_per_cell.derivation: Table I gives 0.0002 mm^2 for 8 arrays: 0.0002 mm^2 / 8 = 25 um^2 per array; / (128 x 128 = 16384 cells) = 1.5259e-3 um^2. Implied cell pitch sqrt(1526 nm^2) = 39.1 nm, i.e. 4F^2 at F = 19.5 nm — a sanity check the number passes.
area_per_cell.note: The source prints ONE significant figure (0.0002 mm^2), so this carries at best one figure of precision despite the arithmetic's five.

area_per_adc.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I, ADC row, p.8
area_per_adc.derivation: 0.0096 mm^2 for 8 ADCs / 8 = 0.0012 mm^2 = 1200 um^2 per 8-bit 1.2 GSps ADC at 32 nm.

area_per_row_driver.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I, DAC row, p.8
area_per_row_driver.note: The paper calls a 1-bit DAC 'a trivial circuit (an inverter)', and 0.17 um^2 is about a minimum-size inverter at 32 nm — the plausibility check this number passes.

area_per_router.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I, Router row, p.8
area_per_router.note: 'Router ... 0.151 (shared by 4 tiles)'. Declared PER ROUTER, so a floorplan with one router per tile over-charges by 4x — ISAAC's c-mesh is concentrated.

area_per_tile_fixed.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I, tile block, p.8
area_per_tile_fixed.derivation: Tile total 0.215 mm^2 minus the tile's router share 0.151/4 mm^2 = 0.17725 mm^2 = 177250 um^2. Components: eDRAM buffer 0.083 + bus 0.090 + sigmoid 0.0006 + S+A 0.00006 + maxpool 0.00024 + OR 0.0032 mm^2.

area_global_fixed.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I, HyperTransport row, p.8
area_global_fixed.note: The off-chip HyperTransport I/O: 4 links at 1.6 GHz, 6.4 GB/s each. Chip total is 85.4 mm^2, of which 62.5 mm^2 is the 168-tile array.

e_mac.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I memristor-array row + Section IV cycle, p.4
e_mac.derivation: Table I publishes POWER, never energy: 2.4 mW x 100 ns = 240 pJ per IMA-cycle; an IMA holds 8 x 128 x 128 = 131072 cells, all activated every cycle; 240 pJ / 131072 = 1.8311 fJ per CELL-MAC.
e_mac.note: Per CELL-MAC (one 1-bit input against one 2-bit cell), which is what the conversion model's synaptic_events counts. A full 16x16 MAC costs 128 of these = 0.234 pJ in the array alone, excluding conversion and periphery.

e_adc_conversion.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I ADC row + Section V 'The Read/ADC Pipeline', p.5
e_adc_conversion.derivation: Operational (nominal): 16 mW x 100 ns = 1.6 nJ per IMA-cycle over 8 arrays x 128 columns = 1024 conversions = 1.5625 pJ. Nameplate (high): 2 mW per ADC / 1.2 GSps = 1.667 pJ. The two agree because the text's actual rate is 1.28 GSps.
e_adc_conversion.note: The single most important constant in this profile: at ~1 conversion per 16-bit MAC, conversion is the dominant analog cost.

t_adc_conversion.citation: shafiee2016isaac Section V + Table I, p.5
t_adc_conversion.derivation: Text rate 1/1.28 GSps = 0.781 ns; Table I nameplate 1/1.2 GSps = 0.833 ns. Cross-checked by the text's own '128 bitline currents are processed in 100 ns' = 0.781 ns each.

e_row_drive.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I DAC row, p.8
e_row_drive.derivation: 4 mW x 100 ns = 400 pJ per IMA-cycle / 1024 rows = 0.3906 pJ per 1-bit row activation.

t_array_read.citation: shafiee2016isaac Section IV 'The ISAAC Pipeline', p.4
t_array_read.note: 'a cycle is the time required to perform one crossbar read operation, which for most of our analysis is 100 ns'. The band's upper end is the paper's own sensitivity point: 'if crossbar latency is assumed to be 200 ns, throughput is reduced by 2x'.

t_cycle.note: 'the cycle time (100 ns) dictated by the slowest stage, which is the crossbar read'. Same quantity and band as t_array_read: in ISAAC the pipeline stage IS the crossbar read.

conductance_levels.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I and Section VIII-A, p.9
conductance_levels.note: 'bits per cell / 2' — 4 conductance states. 'We empirically estimated that the CE metric is maximized when using 2 bits per cell (w = 2).' A 16-bit weight therefore spans 8 cells in adjacent columns, which is the cells_per_weight the conversion model declares.

adc_sharing_factor.derivation: '128 bitline currents are latched in 128 sample-and-hold circuits. In the next 100 ns cycle, these analog values ... are fed sequentially to a single 1.28 GSps ADC unit' — all 128 columns of an array share one ADC. Confirmed by Table I: 8 arrays, 8 ADCs per IMA.

membrane_bits.note: 'We target 16-bit fixed-point arithmetic'. ISAAC is a value-domain accelerator with no membrane state; this is the accumulator width its shift-and-add pipeline carries.

e_intra_tile_packet.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I bus row + Section VI, p.6
e_intra_tile_packet.derivation: 7 mW x 100 ns = 700 pJ per tile-cycle over a bus sized to move 'up to 1KB of data from eDRAM to IR within a 100 ns stage': 700 pJ / 1024 B = 0.6836 pJ per byte moved on-tile.

e_dma_per_byte.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I eDRAM-buffer row, p.8
e_dma_per_byte.derivation: 20.7 mW x 100 ns = 2.07 nJ per tile-cycle / 1024 B = 2.0215 pJ per byte read from the tile's eDRAM buffer.
e_dma_per_byte.note: The ON-CHIP payload cost. The off-chip HyperTransport figure (406 pJ/B) is deliberately NOT used here: the paper states that power is constant rather than activity-proportional, so it belongs in p_static_global instead.

e_program_per_byte.derivation: [TS6] ISAAC is an inference architecture: it preloads its weights and publishes no write energy, and its own e_dma_per_byte (2.0215 pJ/B) prices MOVING a byte through the tile's eDRAM buffer, not committing it to a cell. An analog conductance is committed by a program-and-verify pulse sequence, which the RRAM literature places one to two orders of magnitude above an SRAM write. This library's SRAM class - loihi 28.904, truenorth 22.502, odin 20.6492 pJ/B - has geometric mean 23.7699 pJ/B, so the band is [10x, 100x] that = 237.699 - 2376.99 pJ/B, with the nominal at the band's log-space centre, sqrt(237.699 x 2376.99) = 751.67 pJ/B. Per 2-bit cell (4 cells to the byte) that is 59.4 - 594.2 pJ, the hundreds-of-pJ program-verify scale.
e_program_per_byte.note: ENDURANCE IS UNMODELED. This constant prices the ENERGY of a write and says nothing about the wear it causes: an analog array reprogrammed per inference has a finite write budget (the device literature spans 10^6 - 10^9 cycles), and no quantity in this framework counts writes against it. A workload that reprograms this target per sample is therefore PRICED here but not feasibility-checked. The widest band in the profile, deliberately: the device spread is real and the ratio, not a measurement, is what is known.

t_program_per_byte.derivation: [TS6] The paper states no configuration interface, so the wall is DONOR-SCALED from the two profiles that declare one, along validity.technology_node_nm: truenorth 800 ns/B at 28 nm becomes 800 x 32/28 = 914.286 ns/B, and generic_estimated_22nm 4 / 80 / 1000 ns/B at 22 nm becomes 5.81818 / 116.364 / 1454.55 ns/B. The band is the ENVELOPE of both scaled donors, 5.81818 - 1454.55 ns/B, and the nominal is the geometric mean of their scaled nominals, sqrt(914.286 x 116.364) = 326.174 ns/B.
t_program_per_byte.note: TRANSPORT only, and therefore a LOWER bound on this target: the program-verify pulse sequence that actually settles a conductance is a per-cell wall the device literature puts at the microsecond scale, and it is NOT in this donor-scaled figure - the same modelling gap e_program_per_byte's endurance note names.

e_core_program.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I eDRAM-buffer row, p.8 - through this profile's e_dma_per_byte
e_core_program.derivation: [TS6] ISAAC declares no e_core_init, and its 'core' is a TILE rather than a neuron array, so the neuron-sweep anchor the digital profiles use does not apply. The payload-independent per-tile control work is anchored instead on the tile's own eDRAM buffer cycle - the very quantity e_dma_per_byte divides: 2.0215 pJ/B x 1024 B = 2.07 nJ per tile-cycle. The ratio band [0.5x, 2x] gives 1.035 - 4.14 nJ, with the nominal at the band's log-space centre, 2.07 nJ.
e_core_program.note: Charged per program LOAD (x reprogrammed_cores), and it prices the tile's CONTROL work only - the conductance writes themselves are e_program_per_byte's, endurance caveat included.

p_static_global.citation: shafiee2016isaac Table I HyperTransport row + Section VII, p.7
p_static_global.note: 'The HT is a constant overhead of 10 W, representing half of DaDianNao chip power, but only 16% of ISAAC chip power.' Explicitly CONSTANT, not activity-proportional, which is exactly why it is modelled as static power rather than as a per-byte transport energy.

host_compute_rate.derivation: identity: a measured host wall is used at face value (wall / 1.0)
host_compute_rate.note: The derate a MEASURED host wall is divided by. Identity by definition: this framework measures its host ComputeOp walls end-to-end on the deployment host (StageTimer), and derating a measurement would invent headroom. [H5] Declared here after the loihi precedent because its absence refused the record-plane e2e/energy headlines BY NAME on runs whose host wall was in fact measured.
